page.prose:
Mr. President,

The count is not yet where either of us would like it. I believe the doubtful members will follow the Speaker once the Senate has acted, but I would not stake the session on it.

I shall report again when the last of the committee chairmen has been seen.

reply.prose:
Mr. President,

I have taken the bill and passed it on to committee, as you asked.

setting.situation: Autumn 1941. Britain stands, the Soviet Union is falling back on Moscow, and the United States is neutral in law and not in fact.
sides: The Allies: Britain, the Soviet Union, and the United States in all but name
The Axis: Germany and Italy, with Japan pressing in the Pacific
crawl: It is the autumn of 1941. German armies stand before Moscow.
In the Atlantic, American destroyers escort British convoys as far as Iceland, and U-boats wait beyond.
In Washington, a neutral nation argues about how neutral it means to stay.
facts: The Neutrality Act still bars armed merchant ships.
The draft was renewed by one vote in August.

dates.what: USS Kearny is torpedoed off Iceland.

dossier.bio: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, thirty-second President, in his third term. Crippled by polio at thirty-nine, he governs from a wheelchair the public rarely sees.
dossier.arena: Your arena is Washington and the western Atlantic. Congress decides whether merchant ships may be armed.
history: Asked Congress to arm merchant ships in October 1941.
Ordered the Navy to shoot on sight after the Greer incident.
dossier.quote: We must be the great arsenal of democracy.
dossier.fact: He held 337 press conferences in his first term.
